scores.planner: Proposal 1: offcanvas-lg drawer opened from the header
scores.reasoning: It keeps every brief contract by letter. The header still holds five `button` elements, because the toggle is a link. The panel is the one `.sticky-lg-top` element, so `#offset` writes the same two inline properties and integration.test.ts:1210-1222 holds. `gx-5` keeps the 3rem horizontal gutter, so the main column's width holds, and the 8 px landing holds. It renders no dialog and no backdrop, so J8's `countDialogs` and `collectOverlays` (setupBrowser.ts:1323-1350) read empty. The engine never binds a panel that lacks `.offcanvas` (plugins.ts:246-269, verified). Its co-change list is the most complete of the three. It loses a contracts point in two places. Its Native slot omits the census exemption (sections/integration.test.ts:113) and the never-empty rule. It never names the move in the preservation `excluded` field: `offcanvas-lg`, `offcanvas-start` and `btn` are component names outside main (integration.test.ts:1376-1378). For mobile it has the right pattern: an overlay under a sticky toggle that folds on pick, with Escape returning focus. Two defects hold the score down: a link toggle ignores Space, and frozen tooltips (1080) and popovers (1070) paint over its 1045 drawer. It changes no section frame. Its 9-hour estimate is light for five fold routes, an observer and 16 co-change sites. On risk: the asynchronous marker on `py-1` links makes the partition row depend on timing. Frozen tips can block J3's clicks at 390. Its 692 of 744 px estimate at 768 is optimistic against the journal's button widths.

scores.planner: Proposal 2: sticky details bar with section frames and paint isolation
scores.reasoning: It leaves the header untouched and keeps one inline-style element by making the region itself `.sticky-lg-top`. Its co-changes are correct but wide. The 390 landing moves to 8 px under the bar, which retitles a cited case and moves the setup census landing. `collectContrastSubjects` becomes async with a fifth subject, so every `VARIANT contrast` row moves. `createSection` gains a heading row, which rewrites four factories pins. A Native group after Tailwind needs the variant-case and census edits, which it names. It claims the drawer opens over the page, but the region is sticky and in flow, so opening it grows the region and pushes main down (its own first risk). For mobile, the bar is reachable from any scroll position and uses native `summary` semantics. Against that, the bar grows in flow by up to the viewport height and adds 41 px of permanent chrome. Its isolation is the strongest of the three. Chapter and section frames give each section its own frame. Its paint finding is verified: tooltips.html:57 and popovers.html:50 are `position-relative` with z-index 1080 and 1070 and no stacking ancestor, and z-index.html:7 ties the header's z-index of 3 and paints later. So specimens paint over the sticky header at 9fb2be1. Its Default and Opt-in pair row and its never-empty rule are sound. Effort is 18 hours plus five rulings. On risk, it moves the most baselines (72 heading rows, every caption chip, the `h2` classes and the contrast rows) and changes the scroll-padding semantics.

scores.planner: Proposal 3: in-flow details with section rules
scores.reasoning: It keeps the header, `Showcase.ts`, `createSection`, the contrast subjects, the 8 px landing and both nav-parent pins exactly as they are. Every claim I checked holds. The seven Contents click sites are setupBrowser.ts:3831, :4110, :4489, :4509, :4718, :5202 and :5796. Several suites run at the 414 px default viewport. `getByRole` cannot find a `summary`, while `clickDisclosure`, `readRole` and `readStates` read it (@orkestrel/test 0.0.24, index.js:544-563 and :1145). A group after Tailwind breaks the variant case (integration.test.ts:1152-1156). A top rule breaks the 8 px landing for 63 sections. For mobile it fixes only the arrival. The folded index sits in flow at the top, so past the first screen the reader must scroll back to reach it. It also stays open after a pick and has no motion. For isolation it adds a bottom rule per section at no width cost. Its Native slot inside Interactions avoids census edits, but it is not the separate group the ask names. Effort is 8 hours with no script. Its risk is low: the design is native and synchronous, and the only moved rows are the predicted partition rows and J3's margin.

grafts: From proposal 1: the overlay panel `div#contents-panel.offcanvas-lg.offcanvas-start.sticky-lg-top.vh-100.overflow-y-auto.px-4.px-lg-0.py-3` becomes the single `.sticky-lg-top` element and replaces proposal 3's in-flow drawer. The existing `#offset` writes then place the drawer under lg and bound the sidebar from lg, with no added inline style.

From proposal 1: the toggle sits in the sticky header. The drawer has five fold routes (a link pick, Escape with focus returned to the toggle, focusout to an element outside, a click outside, and the viewport reaching lg). There is no trap, dialog role or backdrop, and no back-to-contents controls.
From proposal 1: `row gx-5`, the `row row-cols-2 row-cols-lg-1 g-3 gx-lg-0` drawer grid, the `contents-drawer` capture state, and the steps of the added drawer case.

From proposals 2 and 3: the toggle is a native `summary`, which gives role `button` through `readRole`, Enter and Space, collapsed and expanded through `readStates`, and `clickDisclosure`. It replaces proposal 1's `a.btn` link.

From proposal 2: `z-0` on every specimen card body whose descendants resolve a z-index of 3 or more at rest, unless it holds a live dropdown, modal or offcanvas, proven by a hit-order case. The drawer needs it, and it also fixes the header overpaint at 9fb2be1.
From proposal 2: the Native pair-row convention, which pairs Default and Opt-in figures with caption badges, variant-named openers and their own tables, and the rule that the group never lands empty.
From proposal 2, reduced: a chapter rule that reads stronger than a section rule, made by adding `border-primary` to the existing group-heading rule.
From proposal 3: a bottom rule (`pb-4 border-bottom`) on every section except its group's last, applied in the members map of `createShell`. `createSection` and the 8 px landing stay as they are.

From proposal 3: the `openContents` and `clickContents` seam covering all seven click sites and the callers at the 414 px default viewport, plus the predicted-difference journey compare that refuses any other difference.

From proposal 1 for the placement and proposal 3 for the census: the Native group sits between `interactions` and `tailwindcss`, so `collectBootstrapGroups` and the variant expectation need no edit, and its census exemption joins `LIVE_GROUP` as a set.
refuted: Proposal 1 claims that the drawer cannot collide with anything and that only a top-layer dialog or a promoted float paints over it. This is incomplete. The frozen `.tooltip.show.position-relative` (tooltips.html:57, z-index 1080) and `.popover.show.position-relative` (popovers.html:50, 1070) have no stacking ancestor, so they paint over a 1045 drawer. With the viewport over those sections, a drawer link can be blocked and J3's `userEvent.click` at 390 fails. The proposal has no co-change for this; the paint-isolation unit fixes it.

Proposal 1's 768 px estimate of 692 of 744 px is too low. The light-390 journal (tmp/journey/light-390.txt) records the Stylesheets group at 353.3 px and Light plus Dark at 104.2 px. Adding a brand near 184 px and a `btn-sm` Contents control near 76 px brings the row within a few pixels of the 744 px bar; those two widths are my estimates, not a run. A wrap under any face would double the 48 px header the guide states. Hiding the version span from md to lg fixes it.

Proposal 1's current-section marker, as specified, makes a journey row depend on timing. An asynchronous IntersectionObserver callback rewrites the class list of Contents links that carry the shared name `py-1`. The partition case keys its `signature coverage` row by every shared-name element's sorted class list (integration.test.ts:1777-1786), so the row depends on whether the callback ran first. The proposal adds only a wait if a row moves. It is deferred.

Proposal 1 claims that a `native` group adds its label and links with no shell change and that its leaf specimens get their own tables. Two co-changes are missing. The section census requires every section outside `interactions` to own an `OWNERSHIP` row (sections/integration.test.ts:113). An empty `GROUPS` entry fails both the variant case, which expects `group-native` (integration.test.ts:1152-1156), and the `:scope > div` count (factories.test.ts:890). The unit that lands the group must make both co-changes.

Proposal 2 claims the drawer 'opens over the page'. This is false. The region is `position-sticky` and in flow, so opening the `details` element grows the region by up to the viewport height and pushes `main` down. Chromium's scroll anchoring then decides how far the visible content shifts, as the proposal's own first risk admits.

Run these steps in order, inside `flock /home/user/.wave/journey.lock`:
1. Run the gates.
2. Run a baseline journey at the branch tip before U1 and a candidate journey on the unit tree, then `compare.ts`.
3. Run `CAPTURE=1 npm run test:journey` and one capture read of `arrival`, `contents-drawer`, `contents-index`, `group-rhythm`, `tooltips` and `popovers` at 390 and 1280.
4. Run `npm run build`, then `npm run build:showcase` twice.
5. Commit the page with the unit.
6. Push the branch, then push `origin/main` by refspec.
7. Republish a private Artifact that holds the committed bytes.
8. Append a lanes entry.
